questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to become a head chef
How photos of food on social media affect what we eat
Why restaurant food is getting more expensive
How to cook healthy meals at home
questions.why: Neil says they are talking about photographing food, which is now big business on social media.

questions.q: When does Rob admit he takes photos of his food?
options: Every time he eats
Only when he cooks at home
Only at a posh restaurant
Never, because he thinks it's a silly thing to do
questions.why: Rob says he has done it, 'but only when eating some amazing food at a posh restaurant'.

questions.q: What does Neil think about the idea of 'style over substance'?
options: Food sometimes tastes just as good as it looks
Beautiful food never tastes good
It is the most important thing for restaurants
It only matters for expensive food
questions.why: Neil says 'Maybe... although I'm sure sometimes the food tastes just as good as it looks.'

questions.q: According to Rebecca Milford, how do her friends now choose what to eat?
options: By reading a restaurant's website
By asking the waiter
By reading long reviews of the restaurant on food blogs
By looking at its photos on Instagram
questions.why: She says they go to the restaurant's Instagram account and choose based on the images.

questions.q: Why do some restaurants pay PR companies?
options: To write their menus
To take stylish food photos for social media
To train their chefs
To find new customers by phoning people at home
questions.why: Neil says some restaurants pay PR companies a lot to take stylish photos to share online.

questions.q: What have some chefs and restaurant owners done, according to Rob?
options: Stopped customers taking photos
Made their portions bigger
Opened new restaurants that only take bookings through Instagram
Changed menus so dishes look good on camera
questions.why: Rob says some have adjusted their menus to produce meals that look good on a smartphone camera.

questions.q: According to Professor Charles Spence, what happens when food is beautifully presented?
options: We expect more, so it seems to taste better
We eat it more slowly
We are less hungry
We are more likely to be disappointed when we taste it
questions.why: He says beautiful presentation 'sets better expectations' which carry over into the tasting experience.

questions.q: Why does Spence say our brain matters before we taste food?
options: It decides how hungry we are
It remembers how much the dish cost on the menu
It already imagines how the food will taste
It warns us if the food is bad
questions.why: He says we see the food first and 'our brain's already imagining what it's going to taste like'.
